quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, use both brakes when needed, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges. These surfaces have less grip than normal pavement.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, make sure you can see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Position your mirror so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane to your side. A properly adjusted mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but the main goal is to see the road behind and to the side of you.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface that makes motorcycles hard to control?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like food and drinks. This means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect you right away.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect you right away.
questions.explanation: Because alcohol does not need digestion, it enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body eliminates alcohol slowly—about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Don't matter much because motorcycles are small.
Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Should not be used if no vehicles are nearby.
Are harder to use than signals on cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are at higher risk, so use your turn signals every time you change lanes or turn. Use them even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and help them see you.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and help them see you.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It also helps you avoid wind from other vehicles, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can be more visible by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: To help others see you, wear bright-colored clothing with reflective material. Always keep your headlight on, and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: Which of the following does not protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: A snug-fitting baseball cap
questions.explanation: Proper protection includes a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Your friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle. You should:

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have been drinking. Stop them however you can, even by taking their keys. Help arrange another way for them to get home.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers a passenger is on board.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Do not carry a passenger unless your motorcycle has a seat large enough for two riders. The motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: Common drugs like cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect your ability to ride safely.
Usually won't affect your ability to ride safely.
Pose no risk to your riding ability.
Are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Learn about the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: Which of the following is not important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects like cracks or loose padding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks cool.
questions.explanation: To get maximum protection, check that your helmet meets U.S. DOT and state standards, fits snugly all the way around your head, and has no obvious defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Ride within one foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Signal only when you feel like it.
Stay alert and be ready to act to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to act to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces give poor tire grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil spots, and metal plates are more hazardous than dry pavement.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you:

options.text: When stopping will be harder than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver ahead from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than usual.
questions.explanation: You need more space when your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Leave more distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: For maximum protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.correctAnswerText: U.S. Department of Transportation.
questions.explanation: For maximum protection, wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not wear a jacket if it is warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. A jacket protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black lettering show road rules like speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following should you check before every ride?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, inspect your motorcycle. Check the tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Mirror checks should:

options.text: Be part of your normal driving routine.
Be avoided because they distract you.
Be avoided because other drivers can see you easily.
Only be done in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be part of your normal driving routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often for safety. You need to know what is behind you. Make mirror checks a regular habit while driving.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
Near the shoulder side of the lane.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually, this means riding in the center of the lane. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on slippery surfaces. Use both brakes when braking and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You are preventing other drivers from entering your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors. This position increases your chance of being seen.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should always scan the road ahead for:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Scan ahead to watch for changing traffic, hazards on the road, and ways to escape danger. Be ready to react to any changes.
